Hi Maya — great to hear, and glad the demo was useful.

High-level answers up front (we'll put a short ops matrix below and attach a DPA excerpt):

- BYOK: Yes — we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for private deployments. Keys are never imported into Redwood-managed HSMs; instead we support an encrypted wrap/handshake and can integrate with your KMS (Azure Key Vault) via a dedicated key-handover protocol. For POC we can do a key-wrap approach so Redwood never stores unwrapped keys.

- Subprocessors: Core infra (Azure compute/storage), telemetry agent (TelemetryCo), and a managed-monitoring vendor (PagerPulse). None of the listed subprocessors will process unredacted plaintext. We'll provide a full subprocessors list in the DPA appendix.

- Operator access: Default is zero access to plaintext and model artifacts. Operator actions that touch KV caches or logs are telemetry-only and masked by default. Break-glass is possible but requires an auditable approval flow, time-limited session, and you keep a copy of the wrapped key for verification.

- Cross-border transfers: By default data and logs remain in your US region. Any exception would require a documented, signed addendum.

I'll attach a short PDF snippet of our DPA and an initial operations matrix. Kimberly, can you confirm the telemetry retention window and subprocessors list for the POC?

1) Kimberly to confirm technical appendix (telemetry retention, subprocessors, operator playbook).

3) Quick 30m call to align on KMS handshake window.

Our proposed technical appendix (concise):

- BYOK options (POC):
  * Key-wrap handshake: customer retains root key; we accept a wrapped key and store only wrapped material. No unwrapped key leaves customer KMS.
  * Optional HSM-attested flow for later production (HSM session attestations, mutual TLS).

- Subprocessors (POC scope):
  * Microsoft Azure (compute, storage) — processes encrypted blobs and ephemeral KV caches within VPC.
  * TelemetryCo — agent for performance metrics; only aggregates and masked traces.
  * PagerPulse — incident monitoring (alerts only; no request payload retention).

- Operator access policy:
  * Normal ops: no access to plaintext requests or model outputs. Operator interfaces only surface anonymized telemetry and per-route latency/cost metrics.
  * Break-glass: audible/recorded approval from two Red/Customer approvers; session expires after 1 hour; full audit trail exported to customer-controlled storage.

- Audit & retention:
  * Audit logs: immutable, signed, stored in customer region for 365 days by default.
  * Request traces: masked (PII redaction) and retained 30 days for troubleshooting; retention extendable by contract.

- Cross-border transfers: No replication outside the customer region unless a documented request is signed and countersigned by legal.

Open items for engineering/legal:
- Confirm exact telemetry fields that get redacted by TelemetryCo (we should supply a short schema).
- Draft DPA clause for subprocessor list and break-glass approvals (Tessa/legal to drive).

If this looks good I'll prepare the terse operations matrix we can share with ClearLake security (one-pager).

Thanks,
